alt: Handwritten notes: computational theory covers language, automata and grammar. The nested circles show regular language inside context free language, inside context sensitive language, inside recursively enumerable language.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten list of language operands: symbols, alphabets (a finite set of inputs such as {a, b, c}), strings (a collection of alphabets) and language (a collection of strings). A regular expression has operands and operations.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten list of regular expression operations: sigma is the input alphabet, a finite set such as {a, b}; epsilon is the empty string; phi is the empty set; plus or union means either a or b; dot is concatenation, so a dot b gives ab.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten notes on the Kleene closure or Kleene star: a plus gives {a, aa, aaa, ...} and a star gives {epsilon, a, aa, aaa, ...}.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten two-column table of regular expressions and the languages they stand for: epsilon gives {epsilon}, phi gives the empty set, a+b gives {a, b}, a.b gives {ab}, a* gives {epsilon, a, aa, ...} and (a.b)* gives {epsilon, ab, abab, ...}.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten definition of a finite state machine or automaton: a finite set of states Q that accepts a finite set of inputs sigma. Its tuples are Q (states), sigma (inputs), delta (transition function Q x sigma to Q), q0 (start state) and F (final state), with a small q0 to q1 transition drawing.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten tree: FSM or FSA in morphology is about creating or making words. Morphology splits into stem (root words) and affixes (prefix, infix, suffix).
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten automata for the stem success: q0 to q1 on the stem success; prefix un then stem success; stem success then suffix ful; and un, success, ful in sequence giving unsuccessful.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten automata for the stem friend: friend alone; prefix un then friend giving unfriend; friend then suffix ly giving friendly; and un, friend, ly in sequence giving unfriendly.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten automata for the stem do: do alone; un then do giving undo; do then able giving doable; and un, do, able in sequence giving undoable.

alt: Handwritten automata for the stem break: break alone; un then break; break then able; and un, break, able in sequence giving unbreakable.
